DIAGNOSIS: New-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus presenting with severe hyperglycemia without ketoacidosis, likely precipitated by an acute stressor (occult infection or physiologic stress) in a patient with underlying essential hypertension.

1. Transient stress hyperglycemia from an occult infection (e.g., urinary tract, skin/soft tissue) not yet identified
2. Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state (HHS), early/impending without frank altered mentation
3. Secondary diabetes from an undisclosed medication (e.g., corticosteroids) or other endocrinopathy (e.g., Cushing's, acromegaly)
